name: Ariel
title: The Little Mermaid makes a splash
text: Disney's The Little Mermaid opened in November 1989. Two years later Ariel was given to more than 5,400 girls, roughly 8x the mid-80s level.

name: Shirley
title: Shirley Temple, box-office queen
text: Shirley was already common, but when child star Shirley Temple broke out in 1934 the name nearly tripled within a year.

name: Deanna
title: From 77 to 1,624 in one year
text: Teen singing star Deanna Durbin's debut 'Three Smart Girls' came out at the end of 1936. Deanna went from 77 babies to 1,624.

name: Tammy
title: Tammy, tammy, tammy's in love
text: Debbie Reynolds' 1957 film and #1 hit 'Tammy' launched a name almost nobody had. By 1960 it was the #31 girls' name in the country.

name: Linda
title: One song, 99,000 Lindas
text: The hit 'Linda' (written for a little girl named Linda Eastman, the future Linda McCartney) helped push Linda to nearly 100,000 babies in 1947 and dethrone Mary.

name: Jaime
title: The Bionic Woman
text: Jaime Sommers got her own TV series in 1976. Girls named Jaime jumped from 914 to 7,838 that year, an 8.6x leap.

name: Farrah
title: The Farrah poster era
text: Charlie's Angels premiered in 1976 and Farrah Fawcett's poster was everywhere. The name rose 18x in two years and was gone again by 1978.

name: Nadia
title: A perfect 10
text: Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics at Montreal in 1976. Nadia went from 86 babies to 585, then 790.

name: Kizzy
title: Roots
text: The 1977 miniseries Roots drew record audiences. Kizzy, the name of Kunta Kinte's daughter, appeared out of nowhere: 1,117 babies, then a fast fade.

name: Katina
title: A soap opera baby
text: Katina went from 95 babies to 2,747 in one year, credited to a newborn character named Katina on the soap 'Where the Heart Is'. Its spelling twin Catina spiked the same year.

name: Woodrow
title: Presidents as namesakes
text: Woodrow Wilson won the 1912 election and the name jumped 15x, peaking in 1918 as the US entered and won WWI.

name: Dewey
title: Hero of Manila Bay
text: Admiral George Dewey's victory in the Spanish-American War made him a national hero in 1898. Dewey jumped 7x that year, then halved every year after.

name: Franklin
title: The FDR bump
text: Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected in 1932. Franklin went from about 1,100 boys a year to 5,363 in 1933.

name: Hillary
title: Peak, then collapse
text: Hillary was climbing for years and peaked in 1992, the year of the Clinton campaign. It then fell 84% in two years: a rare case of a name becoming too strongly tied to one person.

name: Elian
title: A custody battle on every channel
text: The story of Elián González, the six-year-old Cuban boy at the center of a 2000 custody fight, put the name on the map: 23 babies in 1999, 578 in 2000.

name: Selena
title: Remembering the Queen of Tejano
text: After Selena Quintanilla was killed in March 1995, the name quadrupled that year to 3,825 babies.

name: Aaliyah
title: Two spikes, one artist
text: Aaliyah barely existed before the singer's 1994 debut (22 babies in 1993, 1,451 in 1994). After her death in 2001 it spiked again, to 4,779 in 2002.

name: Nevaeh
title: Heaven spelled backwards
text: In 2000, P.O.D. singer Sonny Sandoval introduced his daughter Nevaeh on MTV. A name with 8 babies in 1999 hit 6,800 by 2007.

name: Miley
title: Hannah Montana
text: Miley Cyrus became a Disney Channel star in 2006. Miley went from 26 babies in 2005 to 2,652 in 2008, then faded as she grew up on screen.

name: Bella
title: Twilight
text: Bella Swan of Twilight (book 2005, film 2008) helped push Bella from 2,788 to 5,136 babies in two years.

name: Malia
title: First daughter
text: When the Obamas moved into the White House in 2009, Malia jumped 76% in a single year.

name: Shaquille
title: Shaq attack
text: Shaquille O'Neal went #1 in the 1992 NBA draft and was Rookie of the Year in 1993. Shaquille peaked at 1,785 that year and nearly vanished by 2000.

name: Kobe
title: Remembering Kobe
text: After Kobe Bryant died in January 2020, Kobe tripled from 507 to 1,518 babies that year.

name: Ermias
title: Nipsey Hussle's real name
text: Ermias was Nipsey Hussle's birth name. After he was killed in March 2019, it went from 15 babies to 523.

name: Lionel
title: Messi comes to Miami
text: Messi won the World Cup in December 2022 and joined Inter Miami in July 2023. Lionel rose 35% in 2023 to 609 boys. 'Messi' as a first name never caught on: it never topped 19 babies in a year.

name: Arya
title: Game of Thrones
text: Game of Thrones premiered in 2011. Arya grew 11x by 2019, the year the show ended. Even 'Khaleesi', a title rather than a name, reached 565 girls in 2018.

name: Elsa
title: Let it go
text: Frozen (Nov 2013) doubled Elsa in 2014, then the name fell to below its pre-Frozen level. Parents may have tired of the song.

name: Kylo
title: The dark side
text: Kylo did not exist before Star Wars: The Force Awakens (Dec 2015). It reached 238 boys in 2016 and keeps climbing.

name: Katrina
title: After the hurricane
text: Hurricane Katrina hit in August 2005. The name fell 36% the next year and 74% within four years.

name: Isis
title: An ancient goddess, rebranded
text: Isis, the Egyptian goddess, was steady at about 450 girls a year until 2014. Once 'ISIS' became the common name for the terror group, it fell 89% between 2013 and 2016.

name: Alexa
title: Hey Alexa
text: Amazon launched the Echo in late 2014. Alexa peaked at 6,053 in 2015, then fell 96% as the name became a voice command.

name: Monica
title: 1998's headlines
text: Monica was riding high in the Friends era, then fell by half between 1997 and 1999 as the Lewinsky scandal dominated the news.
